en: Title: *Saṃvarodaya*, Chapter 32 Author: [Scriptural] Source: TUL Matsunami no. 404, folio 95v5–100r1
Now, therefore, I shall explain clearly the reality of the bali offering,
as well as the mandala, fire sacrifice, recitation, consecration, pacification,
nourishment, subjugation, eradication, killing, and the accomplishment of spirits and yakṣiṇīs.
At the time of accomplishing the *pīṭha*, as well as in all rites, this is supreme.
Without the offering of meat (*alibali*), success does not arise quickly;
therefore, offerings (*bali*) are praised, as was spoken by the Buddha of the past.
First, possessing the yoga of the two-armed Saṃvara in the form of the deity,
one should protect oneself with the two protections and resound with the sound of the syllable *hūṃ*. Then,
one should adorn the limbs of the body with [the deities] at the twenty-four sites.
The self whose nature is the yoga of instantaneous form, like a seal of instantaneous form,
instantaneous in every respect— being instantaneous, one should utter the mantra.

First, one should place the food, drink, and so forth before oneself and purify them. Therein, from the syllable *yaṃ* arises a wind-maṇḍala; above that, from the syllable *raṃ*, an fire-maṇḍala; and upon that, from the white syllable *āḥ*, a lotus vessel resting on a hearth formed by three maṇḍalas. In its center, one should produce the food and other items in the form of the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and five lamps (*pañcapradīpa*), presided over by the syllables *oṃ āṃ trāṃ khaṃ hūṃ lāṃ māṃ pāṃ tāṃ caṃ*. One should visualize these seed-syllables melting under the heat of the blazing fire fanned by the wind, becoming a liquid of the color and essence of the newly risen sun. Above that, one should behold the white *khaṭvāṅga*—composed of nectar, with a downward-facing *hūṃ* at its tip, resembling mercury—in a state of melting. One should then see that liquid becoming of one flavor (*samarasībhūta*). Having visualized the syllables *oṃ āḥ hūṃ* produced from the transformation of the vowels and consonants (*āli-kāli*) situated one above the other, and having seen the deities of the maṇḍala-cakra emanated from them perform the welfare of the world, one should meditate as follows: through the process of union (*samāpatti*), they melt and enter into those respective three syllables, remaining there as long as desired. 32.6
Having formed the *agragrahī* [mudrā] with the needle [point] in the middle and firmly applied the *vajra* to the thumbs,
having placed it in the middle at the region of the forehead, one should rotate it, turning it around.
With the feet stepped forward and the gaze directed upward, one should roar "phet" from the head.

When the heroes situated in the ten directions have been drawn in by the Vīrayoginī, she then whirls them with her two right hands toward the assembly of the Ḍākinīs. "You are the pledge! Pledge! Ho! Ho! Ho!"—thus she should cause them to revolve, circling from left to right.
Preceded by the firm conviction (*adhimokṣa*) in the non-duality of the object of worship, the worshipper, and the act of worship,
one should first satisfy the deities, including Indra and his retinue, by summoning them with the syllable *jaḥ*.
In the north, summon Kuvera and his retinue: JAḤ! In the west, summon Varuṇa and his retinue: JAḤ!
In the south, summon Yama and his retinue: JAḤ!

In the northeast, summon the great elements along with their retinues: JAḤ! In the southeast, summon the fires along with their retinues: JAḤ! In the southwest, summon the rākṣasas along with their retinues: JAḤ!

In the northwest, summon the deity Vāyu together with his retinue: JAḤ! Above, summon the moon and sun, Brahmā and the other deities together with their retinues: JAḤ! On the ground below, summon Vemacitrin and the earth deity together with their retinues: JAḤ!

HŪṂ BAṂ HOḤ! All deities are fully satisfied; grant peace and nourishment to the practitioner! May every undertaking be successful; may it be accomplished with ease and happiness as desired! OṂ KARA 2 KURU 2 BANDHA 2 BHRĀMAYA 2 KṢOBHAYA 2 HRO 2 HURU 2 HE 2 PHAṬ 2 DAHA 2 PACA 2 BHAKṢA 2! O you who hang with garlands of fat, blood, and entrails, GRAB 2 the serpent-dragons dwelling in the seven netherworlds, or THREATEN 2 them, and DRAW THEM IN 2! HRĪṂ 2 JÑĀṂ 2 HĀṂ 2 HRĪṂ 2 HŪṂ 2 KILI 2 ŚILI 2 HILI 2 DHILI 2 HŪṂ 2 PHAṬ 2! With this mantra, recited according to the [specific] occasion, one should cause the Lord together with his Wisdom Consort, and the [deities] beginning with the Ḍākinīs and ending with Yamamathanī, to revolve as appropriate. 32.11

"Oṃ vajrāralli jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! O Vajra-Ḍākinīs, you are the pledge; appear, hoḥ! Having presented [the offerings] by reciting this once, twice, thrice, four times, or five times, and having given there one portion each of water for rinsing the mouth, water for sprinkling the hands, and betel, he should satisfy them with the *kamalāvarta* gesture and, after offering praise, make this request:
"Those whose intentions are unshaken by attachment to the equality of existence and peace, who perceive all phenomena as being like space..."
O Goddesses, whose ocean-like minds are overflowing with the waters of profound compassion, bestow, bestow upon me your most intense pity! 32.13

Then, one should cause [the offerings] to be circulated as before for the guardians of the directions and others who dwell in the eight cremation grounds: Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi! May all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, unmādas, apasmāras, and all ḍākas, ḍākinīs, and so forth, accept this bali offering! Protect the pledge! Grant me all accomplishments! Eat, drink, and smell as you wish and according to your pleasure; do not transgress! Be my helpers in every way for the increase of true happiness! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! 32.14

Having praised with the eight-line mantra, one should pray for the attainment of the desired goal. Having signaled with the *chomma* hand gesture, one should recite: "Oṃ, all phenomena are purified by yoga; I am purified by yoga. Having thus satisfied [the deities] with the *kamalāvarta* mudrā, and upon withdrawing the mudrā, one should snap the thumb while enacting the gesture of an embrace.
Oṃ, you have accomplished the welfare of all sentient beings; having granted the attainments as promised, go as you please to the realm of the Buddhas, and may you return again. (32.15–16)
Reciting "Oṃ vajra muḥ," one should dismiss that wheel and cause all [the deities] to enter into one's own self.
Then, afterwards, the collection of the remains of the bali offering must be performed for the sake of attaining the *samaya*.
Having filled the mouth with liquor, one should visualize the flame-mudrā (*jvālāmudrā*).
With a terrible *huṃkāra* sound, one should offer [the remains] into the vessel for leftovers (*ucchiṣṭabhāṇḍaka*).
Having offered flowers, incense, and so forth, and having satisfied [them], one should recite the mantra:
*Oṃ sarvabhakṣa kha kha khāhi 2 ucchiṣṭabalim ucchiṣṭabhaktebhyaḥ svāhā.* (32.19–20)
Endowed with the aesthetic flavors such as compassion, likewise possessing verses of auspiciousness,
completely purified in every aspect of its meaning, and characterized by unchanging great bliss—
the yogin whose nature is wisdom and means accomplishes all activities. 32.21
One should dedicate toward suchness that which is filled with the mind of awakening (bodhicitta),
day after day, month after month, and likewise year after year.

Having fulfilled the supreme desires of the worlds through all forms of giving and so forth, one should grind away the poison of all conceptual delusions by means of the Ḍākinīs, Heruka, and the rest.

And that wheel which, when turned by the Guru Jina, bestows the arising of primordial wisdom and liberation—may it always bring about the supreme welfare of that Great One who is compassionate toward her.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, the Instruction on the Offering of the Bali, from the *Śrīherukābhyudaya*.
